subject: pharmacology
title: Benzodiazepines, Flumazenil and the Z Drugs

steps.tx: **Benzodiazepines** bind a dedicated pocket on the GABA A receptor chloride channel, distinct from GABA itself, and increase the frequency of channel opening when GABA is present, deepening inhibition across cortex, limbic system and spinal cord. Because they need GABA to work and the channel has a conductance ceiling, benzodiazepines alone rarely stop breathing in healthy adults, the safety margin that retired the barbiturates. Alcohol, opioids and other sedatives erase that margin synergistically.
steps.say: Benzodiazepines turn up GABA's volume without playing the instrument themselves; that is their safety margin.

nodes.label: Benzodiazepine binds its GABA A receptor pocket
Channel opening frequency rises where GABA acts
Ceiling effect: GABA presence limits maximal depression

steps.tx: **Benzodiazepines** occupy a site on the GABA A chloride channel that is not the GABA site. They increase opening frequency only while GABA is already bound, which deepens inhibition in cortex, limbic system and spinal cord. They cannot open the channel by themselves, and channel conductance has a ceiling, so a healthy adult rarely stops breathing on a benzodiazepine alone. That ceiling is what allowed these drugs to replace barbiturates. Alcohol, opioids and other sedatives remove the margin when they are taken together.
steps.say: Benzodiazepines bind their own pocket on the GABA A channel and make it open more often only when GABA is present. They do not open the channel alone, and a conductance ceiling remains, so healthy adults seldom stop breathing on these drugs by themselves. Alcohol or an opioid removes that protection.

steps.tx: Individual agents are chosen by half life and metabolism: **diazepam**, long acting with active metabolites, suits alcohol withdrawal tapers and status epilepticus; **lorazepam**, conjugated directly without active metabolites, is the reliable choice in liver disease and the elderly and the preferred intravenous agent for prolonged seizures; **midazolam**, ultra short and water soluble, owns procedural sedation and infusions. The conjugation shortcut (lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam) is the famous LOT trio spared by failing livers.
steps.say: Diazepam lasts, lorazepam is liver safe, midazolam is brief; the LOT drugs bypass oxidation.

left.title: Long and intermediate agents
points: Diazepam: active metabolites, withdrawal tapers, seizures
Chlordiazepoxide: alcohol withdrawal tradition
Clonazepam: long acting anticonvulsant and panic use
Accumulation in elderly and liver disease

right.title: Liver friendly and short agents
points: Lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam: direct conjugation (LOT)
Midazolam: ultra short, procedural and infusion use
Lorazepam preferred in status epilepticus infusions
All need dose restraint in respiratory disease

steps.tx: In **status epilepticus** a benzodiazepine is the first drug and minutes decide outcome: intravenous lorazepam 4 mg or diazepam 10 mg, buccal or intramuscular midazolam where no vein exists, repeated once before second line levetiracetam, lacosamide or phenytoin loading. Underdosing from fear is the commonest error; the seizure injures brain faster than the sedative injures breathing when airways are attended. Escalation beyond two doses belongs to critical care with anaesthetic infusions.
steps.say: Seizures first, sedative fear second: full dose benzodiazepine early, airway attended, second line loaded next.

nodes.label: Generalised seizure beyond 5 minutes: status epilepticus
Lorazepam 4 mg IV or midazolam buccal or IM
Repeat benzodiazepine once at 5 to 10 minutes
Second line loading, then critical care if refractory

steps.tx: **Chronic use** extracts its price list: tolerance to sedation and anticonvulsion within weeks, physical dependence with withdrawal seizures after months, anterograde amnesia, falls and hip fractures in the elderly, and paradoxical disinhibition in children and dementia. Prescribing discipline therefore means short courses, taper plans, and avoiding the class in sleep apnoea, myasthenia gravis and acute intoxication. Withdrawal tapers convert short acting agents to diazepam equivalents and descend over weeks to months.
steps.say: Weeks bring tolerance, months bring dependence; prescribe with the exit taper already written.

left.title: Costs of chronic use
points: Tolerance to sedation within weeks
Dependence with withdrawal seizure risk
Falls, fractures and cognitive dulling in the elderly
Paradoxical agitation in children and dementia

right.title: Disciplined use
points: Lowest dose, shortest course, review date set
Taper via diazepam equivalents over weeks
Avoid in sleep apnoea and acute intoxication
Non drug insomnia and anxiety therapy first line chronically

steps.tx: **Flumazenil** competitively antagonises the benzodiazepine pocket, reversing sedation within minutes, and is stocked for iatrogenic oversedation after procedures. Its half life of about an hour is shorter than most agonists it reverses, so resedation stalks the recovery ward. In chronic benzodiazepine dependence or mixed tricyclic overdose it can precipitate withdrawal seizures and unmask arrhythmias, which confines it to selected, monitored, usually anaesthetist led indications rather than undifferentiated coma cocktails.
steps.say: Flumazenil reverses for an hour while the sedative lasts all night; dependence turns the antidote into a seizure trigger.

nodes.label: Observe for resedation as flumazenil wanes

steps.tx: The **zolpidem** family, the Z drugs, bind the same GABA A complex at alpha 1 predominant sites, aiming hypnotic selectivity at hypnotic doses with less anxiolytic, anticonvulsant and muscle relaxant spill. Zolpidem and zaleplon (ultra short, for sleep onset) and their cousin eszopiclone next lesson remain dependence forming controlled drugs, not the harmless alternatives marketing promised. Complex sleep behaviours, cooking, driving and eating asleep, forced dose cuts and boxed warnings, particularly in women clearing zolpidem slowly.
steps.say: Z drugs aim at the sleep subunit only; dependence and sleep driving followed them anyway.

left.title: Zolpidem and zaleplon
points: Alpha 1 selective GABA A modulation
Zaleplon ultra short: sleep onset only
Zolpidem lower starting dose in women
Complex sleep behaviours carry boxed warnings

right.title: Shared sedative cautions
points: Dependence and rebound insomnia on stopping
Additive respiratory depression with opioids and alcohol
Falls and next morning impairment in the elderly
Short courses with review, as for benzodiazepines

steps.tx: **Paradoxical reactions** deserve a named step because examinations and wards both meet them: instead of calm, a minority (children, elderly, dementia, brain injury, high dose intravenous use) become agitated, aggressive and disinhibited as cortical brakes release. Management stops the drug rather than escalating it, protects the airway, and chooses antipsychotic or dexmedetomidine strategies where sedation remains essential. Documenting the reaction prevents every future team repeating the experiment.
steps.say: Agitation after a sedative can be the sedative; stop it rather than stacking more.

nodes.label: Benzodiazepine given for sedation or agitation
Worsening agitation and disinhibition instead of calm
Stop the benzodiazepine, protect airway and safety

steps.tx: **Sorting the sedative shelf** by mechanism prepares the barbiturate contrast next lesson: benzodiazepines raise opening frequency and need GABA, barbiturates prolong opening duration and open channels directly at high dose (hence lethal respiratory depression), Z drugs select alpha 1 subunits, and newer agents leave GABA entirely (melatonin agonists, orexin antagonists). Mechanism, not brand familiarity, predicts which overdose has an antidote, a ceiling or neither.
steps.say: Frequency, duration, subunit or new target: the mechanism predicts the overdose story every time.

left.title: GABA A modulators
points: Benzodiazepines: frequency up, GABA required, ceiling
Barbiturates: duration up, direct opening, no ceiling
Z drugs: alpha 1 subunit selectivity
Flumazenil antagonises only the benzodiazepine pocket

right.title: Beyond GABA (next lessons)
points: Ramelteon: melatonin MT1 MT2 agonism
Suvorexant: orexin receptor antagonism
Buspirone: serotonin 1A partial agonism for anxiety
Each trades sedative power for safety in its niche
